descriptionChirho: The passive sense of writing or recording, specifically 'to be inscribed/written down' in official documents or registries. Niphal stem denotes the passive reception of the written act. English 'was-inscribed', Spanish 'fue-inscrita' (was inscribed), Hindi 'likha-gaya-hai' (was written), Arabic 'kutibat' (it was written, passive), Korean 'girokdoen/girokdoeeotdeora' (was recorded), Swahili 'yaliandikwa' (were written). The passive voice is consistent across all target languages, distinguishing this from the active signing sense.

The active sense of signing or writing a document, used in the context of official decrees and edicts (Daniel 6). Qal stem perfect and imperative forms indicating the agent who writes or signs. English 'you-signed/signed/and-sign', Spanish 'firmaste/firmo/y-firma' (you signed/he signed/and sign), Hindi 'tune-likha/likha/aur-likh-de' (you wrote/wrote/and write), Arabic 'katabta/kataba/uktub' (you wrote/he wrote/write!), Korean 'seomyeonghasin/seomyeonghayeotdeora' (you-signed/was-signed), Swahili 'ulitia-sahihi/alitia-sahihi/na-tia-sahihi' (you put signature/he put signature/and put signature).
